speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You have a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation; to start our evaluation, please describe exactly how your mental status has changed and what your highest recorded temperature has been. Also, have you experienced any recent head trauma or seizures?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS). 

I have reviewed your history of fever, altered mentation, and recent use of haloperidol, which are classic signs of NMS. The absence of chills, rigors, or headache further supports this diagnosis over other causes like meningitis or encephalitis.
